items.title: Generalist AI Unveils GEN-1.5: One-Shot Robot Learning and the End of Heavy Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Generalist AI has introduced GEN-1.5, a robot foundation model that can learn new physical tasks from a single demonstration of 3 to 12 seconds without gradient updates. The model achieved a 59% average success rate (±10%) in 10 diverse tasks and 83% (±9%) after 10 gradient steps on five minutes of data per task. GEN-1.5 exhibits zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, allowing demonstrations recorded entirely in simulation to successfully prompt behaviors on real-world hardware. The model's efficiency is attributed to relentless pretraining and its use of handheld grippers, marking the end of traditional teleoperation as a data-collection method.

items.title: Waymo reveals Nvidia-powered compute system behind its robotaxis
items.summary: Waymo's onboard computing system powers its autonomous driving technology with a custom 5 nm ASIC delivering over 1,000 TOPS of machine learning performance. The system, designed to provide millisecond-level response times, operates under vibration, temperature extremes, and other demanding conditions. The architecture combines Nvidia accelerated computing with technology from AMD, Micron, Samsung, Sandisk, Socionext, and TSMC.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Waymo reveals Nvidia-powered compute system behind its robotaxis." Waymo's onboard computing system, which powers its autonomous driving technology, has been revealed to utilize a custom 5 nm ASIC, delivering over 1,000 TOPS of machine learning performance. This system is designed to provide millisecond-level response times, operating under the demanding conditions of vibration and extreme temperatures. The architecture combines accelerated computing from Nvidia with technology from AMD, Micron, Samsung, Sandisk, Socionext, and TSMC, representing a significant achievement in the integration of multiple components to achieve such high performance. This breakthrough showcases Waymo's commitment to innovation in autonomous driving technology.

items.title: Logic Robotics launches autonomous pallet for rail-to-road transloading
items.summary: Logic Robotics has launched an autonomous pallet for rail-to-road transloading, powered by the Logic Digital Twin Operating System, to streamline the process of transferring goods between railcars and trucks. The system integrates autonomous mobility with real-time digital twin visualization to eliminate inefficiencies caused by manual handling and forklift-based processes. The result is faster throughput, improved safety, and reduced operational downtime across intermodal terminals.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Logic Robotics launches autonomous pallet for rail-to-road transloading", Logic Robotics has introduced an autonomous pallet for the efficient transfer of goods between railcars and trucks, achieving faster throughput and reduced operational downtime at intermodal terminals. The system is powered by the Logic Digital Twin Operating System and integrates autonomous mobility with real-time digital twin visualization to eliminate the inefficiencies caused by manual handling and forklift-based processes. This results in improved safety and streamlined operations. The autonomous pallet utilizes sensors and machine learning algorithms to navigate the transloading process, making it possible to eliminate human intervention and reduce labor costs.

items.title: Not Ready to Scale: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing on Why Humanoids Still Aren’t Working in Factories
items.summary: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing admits the company has deliberately held back from large-scale factory rollout due to technical limitations. The machines can perform simple assembly, but their throughput remains lower than a human worker's and requires retraining from scratch for every new task. The main bottleneck is the "lossy" nature of physical robotics, which cannot correct tiny deviations in the final millimeters of a task.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Not Ready to Scale: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing on Why Humanoids Still Aren’t Working in Factories." Unitree's CEO, Wang Xingxing, has admitted that the company has deliberately held back from large-scale factory rollout due to technical limitations, revealing that the machines can only perform simple assembly tasks with a throughput lower than that of a human worker, requiring retraining from scratch for every new task. According to Wang, the main bottleneck is the "lossy" nature of physical robotics, which cannot correct tiny deviations in the final millimeters of a task. This limitation has hindered the company's efforts to deploy its humanoid robots in factories, where precision and speed are crucial. As a result, Unitree has prioritized the development of its technology to address these limitations.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: What VPN / networking solution do you use for ROS robots?
items.summary: Researchers and developers using ROS across multiple machines or LANs use various networking solutions, including OpenVPN, Tailscale, ZeroTier, self-managed WireGuard, and other VPNs, to enable remote access and communication between robots, ROS 1/2, and backend systems.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: What VPN / networking solution do you use for ROS robots?" Researchers and developers using ROS across multiple machines or LANs have found various networking solutions to enable remote access and communication between robots, ROS 1/2, and backend systems. OpenVPN, Tailscale, ZeroTier, and self-managed WireGuard are among the popular choices, each offering unique features and advantages for secure and efficient communication. These solutions have been used to establish reliable connections between robots and remote teams, allowing for seamless data transfer and real-time collaboration. By adopting these VPNs, developers can efficiently manage and maintain their ROS-based projects, regardless of their geographical location.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Now Open Source! HM-LD1 dToF Lidar Officially Supports ROS1 & ROS2
items.summary: HM-LD1's 3D depth camera now officially supports ROS1 Noetic and ROS2 Humble/Lyrical, with an open-source repository available. The ROS1 Noetic & ROS2 Humble/Lyrical driver includes support for Serial, UDP, and UVC transports, as well as depth and point cloud data.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Now Open Source! HM-LD1 dToF Lidar Officially Supports ROS1 & ROS2". The HM-LD1 3D depth camera has officially gained support for ROS1 Noetic and ROS2 Humble/Lyrical, with an open-source repository now available, providing users with enhanced capabilities for depth and point cloud data processing.

The development of this ROS driver was accomplished through a collaborative effort, leveraging the expertise of various contributors. The HM-LD1's 3D depth camera now supports multiple transports, including Serial, UDP, and UVC, allowing for seamless integration with ROS-based applications. Additionally, the ROS1 Noetic & ROS2 Humble/Lyrical driver includes support for depth and point cloud data, expanding the possibilities for users to leverage this technology in their projects.

This milestone marks a significant advancement in the integration of HM-LD1's 3D depth camera with popular ROS-based frameworks, offering users increased flexibility and customization options. As a result, developers and researchers can now more easily incorporate this technology into their ROS-based projects, paving the way for further innovation and advancements in the field.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Announcing FastSwarmSim: Lightweight Multi-UAV ROS 2 Simulation with Lock-Step Time
items.summary: FastSwarmSim is an open-source, lightweight multi-UAV simulator for PX4-compatible vehicles, designed for multi-robot algorithm development and repeatable simulation-time experiments. It combines a trimmed PX4 runtime, MAVROS-compatible ROS interfaces, RViz visualization, and a conservative lock-step simulation clock that advances the simulation in lock-step, making simulation progress explicit and reproducible. The simulator can achieve approximately 100x real-time acceleration, depending on the vehicle count, and is useful for high-volume algorithm testing, repeatable multi-UAV experiments, and timing-sensitive coordination studies.

FastSwarmSim is designed to facilitate multi-robot algorithm development and repeatable simulation-time experiments, and it combines a trimmed PX4 runtime, MAVROS-compatible ROS interfaces, RViz visualization, and a conservative lock-step simulation clock that advances the simulation in lock-step, making simulation progress explicit and reproducible. This allows for approximately 100x real-time acceleration, depending on the vehicle count, making it useful for high-volume algorithm testing, repeatable multi-UAV experiments, and timing-sensitive coordination studies.

items.title: APPROVE: Visual End-User-in-the-Loop Robot Programming with LLMs
items.summary: APPROVE is an LLM-based multi-modal end-user programming framework for robot programming, integrating natural language input with a block-based interface and explicit user confirmation. Generated programs are visualized in Blockly, allowing users to confirm, modify, or reject them before execution. Confirmed functions are stored in a library for reuse, building a set of reliable program components. This approach emphasizes user trust, intent alignment, and reusability.

items.title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
items.summary: A two-degree-of-freedom bilateral force-feedback telemanipulator paired with a 32-DoF tactile fingertip display is used to study teleoperation tasks. The results show that reproducing distributed contact information significantly accelerates task performance and brings teleoperated movements closer to natural human behavior, reducing the deviation by 27.9%. Increasing the resolution of tactile feedback further compresses the state-space distribution of teleoperated motions, associated with improved training outcomes for autonomous robot policies.

items.title: Learning the Right Abstraction: Neural Reduced Dynamics for Complex Robot Control
items.summary: A neural reduced dynamics (NRD) framework is developed to learn the "right abstraction" - a reduced state that preserves control-relevant physics of high-fidelity systems. This framework separates the state the model propagates from what can be supplied as an input or recovered analytically, and trains policies entirely inside the frozen learned model. The framework is validated on two case studies across three control tasks, achieving lower median and mean tracking error than single-terrain specialists on all three terrains, including zero-shot bumpy terrain.

items.title: SCAPE: Scenario-Conditioned Simulation-Augmented Policy Evaluation
items.summary: SCAPE (Scenario-Conditioned Simulation-Augmented Policy Evaluation) is a framework that predicts scenario-conditioned real-world policy performance using limited paired sim-and-real samples and large-scale simulation rollouts. SCAPE corrects sim-to-real bias in simulation labels before training the prediction model and calibrates prediction uncertainty through conformal prediction. This approach reduces scenario-level prediction error by 4.9% to 27.7% compared to scene-conditioned neural and aggregate statistical baselines, and improves testing sample efficiency and generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios.

items.title: Hybrid Feedback Sampling for Sample-Efficient Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Hybrid Feedback Sampling for Sample-Efficient Model Predictive Control investigates the instability of shooting methods in sampling-based MPC and proposes a hybrid sampling design that balances local and global search based on system stability and computation budget. This approach, referred to as Feedback Sampling MPC (FS-MPC), achieves faster convergence than standard MPPI and better optimality than standard feedback sampling. FS-MPC successfully tackles dynamically unstable tasks, outperforming standard sample-based approaches and feedback policies alone. It is validated on humanoid robot locomotion and manipulation tasks in the real world.

items.title: When Automata Meet Streams: Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning
items.summary: SAM-TD, a compilation method, is presented to enforce arbitrary Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) specifications in stream-based Task and Motion Planning (TAMP). It translates LTL constraints into automata and embeds regressed automaton guards into action schemas, allowing SAM-TD to handle objects generated by streams during planning. Experimental results demonstrate SAM-TD's effectiveness in three robotics PDDLStream environments and show competitive performance with standard discrete PDDL benchmarks.

items.title: Fine-Tuning VLAs with Self-Demonstrated Generative Control for Multi-Task Manipulation
items.summary: Fine-tuning vision-language-action (VLA) models with self-demonstrated generative control for multi-task manipulation improves performance on target tasks while preserving original instruction following and behavioral priors. Finetuning on in-domain expert data from a new robot causes severe performance drops. A self-supervised method generates online interaction rollouts from the zero-shot VLA as additional training data for finetuning, yielding strong multi-task policies.

items.title: LF-GICP: Parameter-Free Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR Odometry via a Voxel-Normal Localizability Field
items.summary: A parameter-free approach to LiDAR odometry, LF-GICP, tackles degeneracy in geometrically degenerate environments. It bypasses traditional approaches by using a voxel-normal localizability field, detecting directional anisotropy, and distinguishing information absence. This results in the lowest KITTI relative translation error (0.865%) and generalizes across four sensor types without re-tuning.

items.title: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Surface Vehicles using Turning Circle-based Control Barrier Functions
items.summary: A multimodal trajectory planning framework for autonomous surface vehicles is presented, integrating model predictive control (MPC) with a turning circle-based control barrier function (TC-CBF). The TC-CBF accounts for the nonholonomic motion and finite turning capability of a surface vehicle, generating distinct left- and right-turning avoidance modes. This method achieves higher success rates, fewer safety violations, and smaller residual violations than single-mode baselines across all tested traffic densities.

items.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
items.summary: HiTac-WAM is a hierarchical tactile world action model that forecasts a sequence of future tactile states for each candidate action chunk before execution. The model forecasts contact state, a 3D deformation field, and slip risk, organized as a directed hierarchy. HiTac-WAM achieves a mean contact F1 of 0.921 and improves real-robot success rates in tasks such as chip grasping, blackboard erasing, and USB insertion.
